name: genotype-phenotype-baseline
title: Classical Baselines — Random Forest and Logistic Regression on Synthetic Multi-Omic Data
question: What is the best AUC-ROC and F1 score achievable with classical ML methods on synthetic multi-omic phenotype prediction, to establish a baseline for quantum classifier comparison?
objective:
Train Random Forest and Logistic Regression on synthetic multi-omic data
and report accuracy, AUC-ROC, F1, precision, and recall.
hypothesis: Random Forest will outperform Logistic Regression by capturing nonlinear cross-modality interactions, but both will serve as strong baselines.

study_card.goal: Establish reproducible classical ML baselines for quantum classifier comparison.
study_card.mechanism: Train RF (100 trees, max_depth=8) and LR (C=1.0, max_iter=1000) on the same synthetic multi-omic train/test split used by GenotypeToPhenotypeProcess.
study_card.why_before_next: Every quantum advantage claim must be measured against the best available classical method on identical data.

description: This study trains two classical classifiers on synthetic multi-omic data generated by the same pipeline used in the quantum classifier evaluation. Both classifiers are evaluated on held-out test sets with the same train/test ratio. Results establish the baseline the quantum classifier must beat.
expected_behavior: Random Forest AUC-ROC exceeds 0.80 on synthetic multi-omic test data.
Logistic Regression AUC-ROC exceeds 0.70 on the same test data.
